scope.plan: user-provided Docker daemon status and configuration plan

findings.title: External Docker configuration edits can be overwritten
findings.why_it_matters: A concurrent SSH or other host edit during dockerd validation or a failed restart could be replaced without a fresh revision comparison.
evidence: The original revision was checked only before the asynchronous validation and restart operations.
Rollback replaced the current file without confirming it still matched the transaction pending revision.

findings.title: Package upgrade exposes root recovery material to zos
findings.why_it_matters: The recursive state-directory chown changed the owner of daemon.json baselines that can contain proxy or registry credentials.
evidence: postinst ran chown -R zos:zos /zos/state after the helper stored recovery files below that path.

findings.title: Docker daemon SSE lifecycle lacks coverage
findings.why_it_matters: Timer or deduplication regressions could leak polling work or stop real-time status updates without route-level evidence.
evidence: The initial implementation had no assertions for initial delivery, unchanged samples, heartbeat output, or close cleanup.

findings.title: Daemon API validation and systemd normalization are incomplete
findings.why_it_matters: Malformed revisions could cross the API boundary, and an actively reloading Docker service was presented as failed.
evidence: Only the helper checked the 64-character lowercase SHA-256 revision shape.
normalizeDockerDaemonState handled active but not systemd's reloading active state.

appliedFixes: Added revision compare-before-replace checks across save, restart, and rollback.
Kept daemon recovery state root-owned after package configuration.
Covered SSE initial state, deduplication, heartbeat, and close cleanup.
Aligned API revision validation and systemd reloading normalization.

testingGaps: Exercise the real privileged helper, dockerd validator, and docker.service restart on the Linux deployment target.
residualRisks: SSE systemd sampling is per connected client; the current single-user appliance scope keeps this bounded.

verification: focused helper, API, frontend helper, and packaging tests
invalid JSON, save-pending, restart-confirmation, and rollback UI checks
